evidence: Plin. Ep. 1.20.12: adjiciam quod mē docuit ūsus, magister ēgregius (Lewis & Short s.v. ūsus)
Cic. Rab. Post. 9: sī ūsus magister est optimus, mihi dēbet esse nōtissima (not checked)
terms.comment: Cicero’s words: “if experience is the best teacher”. Not in Lewis & Short or the loci collections; we have not checked the passage.
The saying as a sentence. Every word is classical; we have found no classical instance of the phrase in this form.

terms.gloss: practice, the best teacher of speaking

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, cited by printed page; each phrase checked against the searchable text of the book.
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
